name: Europa Clipper
summary: Investigating whether Jupiter's icy moon Europa has conditions suitable to support life beneath its global saltwater ocean.
quote: “We are voyagers across the dark, seeking an ocean beneath the ice.”
cite: — U.S. Poet Laureate Ada Limón (engraved on the spacecraft vault)
description: Europa Clipper is the largest spacecraft NASA has ever built for a planetary mission. It carries an ice-penetrating radar, high-resolution cameras, an infrared spectrometer, and dust/gas analyzers to perform dozens of close flybys of Europa, mapping its ice shell thickness and scouting for subsurface ocean plumes.

specs.powerSource: Massive 30.5m Solar Arrays (largest ever for deep space)
specs.primaryInstruments: REASON Ice Radar, PIMS Plasma, MASPEX Mass Spectrometer, EIS Cameras

timeline.detail: Successful launch from Kennedy Space Center
High-speed slingshot around Mars
Final orbital acceleration boost
Jupiter Orbit Insertion (JOI)
49 precision flybys down to 25 km altitude

name: Artemis II
summary: First crewed spacecraft to fly beyond low Earth orbit since Apollo 17 in 1972, sending four astronauts around the Moon.
quote: “We are going to live and work in deep space to prepare for the leap to Mars.”
cite: — Artemis II Crew Commander Reid Wiseman
description: Artemis II will carry NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen on a high-stakes 10-day test flight around the far side of the Moon and back, validating Orion's life support systems with humans aboard.

specs.crewSize: 4 Astronauts (including first woman and person of color on lunar mission)

timeline.detail: Core stage assembly at Vehicle Assembly Building
Liftoff from Launch Pad 39B
Manual proximity operations & life support checkout
Loop around lunar far side beyond radio horizon
High-speed 40,000 km/h atmospheric reentry

name: Dragonfly
summary: A nuclear-powered rotorcraft that will fly between organic dunes and impact craters on Saturn's giant moon Titan.
quote: “Titan has all the ingredients needed for life—frozen in prebiotic time.”
cite: — Dr. Elizabeth Turtle, Dragonfly Principal Investigator
description: Dragonfly will be humanity's first multi-rotor vehicle to fly scientific payloads across an alien world. Capitalizing on Titan's dense nitrogen atmosphere and one-seventh Earth gravity, the drone will hop tens of kilometers between landing sites to examine prebiotic chemistry in organic sand dunes and the Shangri-La impact crater.

specs.sciencePayload: DraMS Mass Spectrometer, DraGNS Gamma-Ray Spectrometer, Seismometer

timeline.detail: Aeroshell & autonomous flight testing
Departure from Earth
6-year trajectory to Saturnian system
Parachute descent through Titan's golden smog
3+ years of aerial exploration across Titan

name: Artemis III
summary: Humanity's return to the surface of the Moon, targeting the water-ice laden craters of the lunar South Pole.
quote: “We are going to step onto a world where water ice has waited billions of years for us.”
description: Artemis III will mark the first human footsteps on the Moon in more than half a century. Two crew members will descend to the rugged lunar South Pole in a commercial Human Landing System (Starship HLS), conducting moonwalks in permanently shadowed craters to sample primordial water ice.

specs.landingSite: Permanently shadowed crater rims at Lunar South Pole
specs.spacesuits: Axiom Space Next-Gen Extravehicular Mobility Unit (AxEMU)
specs.scienceGoals: Water-ice core sample extraction, volatile analysis, cold-trap prospecting

timeline.detail: Propellant transfer in low Earth orbit
SLS launches Orion crew to lunar orbit
Descent to South Pole landing site
4 EVA excursions collecting ice and rock samples
Docking with Orion and splashdown on Earth

name: Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope
summary: NASA's next flagship observatory with a field of view 100 times greater than Hubble, surveying dark energy and billions of galaxies.
quote: “Hubble gave us a microscope; Roman will give us a wide-angle lens on the cosmic tapestry.”
cite: — Dr. Julie McEnery, Roman Senior Project Scientist
description: Equipped with a 2.4-meter mirror and a 300-megapixel Wide Field Instrument, Roman will map the large-scale distribution of dark matter and dark energy, hunt for microlensed exoplanets in the galactic bulge, and test high-contrast starlight-blocking coronagraph technology to image alien solar systems directly.

specs.fieldOfView: 100x Hubble Space Telescope view per image
specs.scienceFocus: Dark Energy equation of state, Exoplanet census, Infrared galactic survey

timeline.detail: Cryogenic thermal vacuum chamber certification
Final instrument mating at Goddard Space Flight Center
SpaceX Falcon Heavy launch from Florida
Commissioning 1.5 million km from Earth
Scanning billions of galaxies across cosmic time

name: JUICE (JUpiter ICy moons Explorer)
summary: Europe's flagship mission to study Ganymede (the largest moon in the Solar System) and its massive sub-surface ocean.
quote: “Ganymede is the only moon with its own magnetic shield—protecting a deep saltwater sea.”
description: JUICE is currently cruising across the solar system, having performed the first-ever Lunar-Earth gravitational assist flyby. In 2031, it will enter orbit around Jupiter before eventually entering orbit around Ganymede—making it the first spacecraft ever to orbit a moon other than our own.

specs.destination: Ganymede, Callisto, and Europa ocean systems
specs.powerSource: 85 square meters of solar panels (massive cross wings)
specs.payload: 10 state-of-the-art instruments including JANUS camera and RIME radar
specs.milestone: First spacecraft to orbit a moon around another planet

timeline.detail: Ariane 5 liftoff from Kourou, French Guiana
World-first lunar-terrestrial gravity brake
Solar system interior slingshot
Enter Jovian orbital resonance
Dedicated low-altitude orbit around Ganymede

name: Mars Sample Return (MSR)
summary: Retrieving the rock and soil core samples drilled by Perseverance and rocketing them back to laboratories on Earth.
quote: “The only way to answer whether life existed on Mars is to bring the rocks home.”
cite: — Mars Sample Return Independent Review Board
description: Perseverance has already cached dozens of hermetically sealed titanium sample tubes in Jezero Crater. Mars Sample Return will land a rocket (Mars Ascent Vehicle) on Mars, collect the sample cache, launch into Martian orbit, and rendezvous with an Earth Return Orbiter to bring the tubes home for mass spectrometry analysis.

specs.components: Sample Retrieval Lander, Mars Ascent Vehicle (MAV), Earth Return Orbiter
specs.sampleCount: Up to 30 titanium sample tubes filled with core sediments
specs.returnFacility: Bio-safety Level 4 Curation Facility on Earth
specs.historicFirst: First rocket launch from the surface of another planet

timeline.detail: Perseverance seals core samples in Jezero delta
Launch of Mars Ascent Vehicle
First rocket liftoff from Martian soil into orbit
Autonomous sample transfer to Earth Return Orbiter
Pristine sample capsule recovery in Utah desert

name: VERITAS & DAVINCI
summary: Returning to Earth's runaway greenhouse twin to map its volcanic continents and drop an atmospheric descent probe.
quote: “Venus is Earth's sister world—learning why it turned into hell tells us how our own planet stays alive.”
description: VERITAS will orbit Venus with synthetic aperture radar to map global topography and identify active volcanism. DAVINCI will plunge a titanium descent sphere through Venus's crushing 90-atmosphere sulfuric acid skies, measuring atmospheric noble gases and photographing mountain tesserae before touching the scorching 460°C surface.

specs.instruments: VISAR Radar, VEM Emissivity Mapper, VMS Mass Spectrometer
specs.focus: Why did Venus lose its oceans and suffer runaway greenhouse warming?

timeline.detail: Final hardware specifications
Aerobraking entry into Venusian orbit
63-minute parachute descent to Alpha Regio
Sub-kilometer global geological map of Venus

name: Psyche Mission
summary: Exploring a metal-rich asteroid that may be the exposed iron-nickel core of an early planetary building block.
quote: “We have visited worlds of rock, ice, and gas—now we visit a world of metal.”
cite: — Dr. Lindy Elkins-Tanton, Psyche Principal Investigator
description: Psyche is journeying 3.6 billion kilometers into the outer asteroid belt using advanced solar electric Hall-effect thrusters. Unlike rocky or icy bodies, asteroid 16 Psyche appears to consist largely of exposed metallic nickel and iron, giving scientists an unprecedented glimpse into the molten interior cores of terrestrial planets like Earth.

specs.laserCommunications: DSOC Deep Space Optical Laser Transceiver (tested at 460M km)

timeline.detail: SpaceX Falcon Heavy liftoff
Streamed 4K cat video & data from deep space via laser
Orbital velocity boost
Entering orbit around the metal world

name: Lucy
summary: First mission to explore Jupiter's Trojan asteroid swarms—ancient planetary fossils locked at the L4 and L5 Lagrange points.
quote: “Looking back in time to the primordial material that assembled our planets.”
description: Over a 12-year odyssey, Lucy will visit an unprecedented record of eight asteroids: two main-belt asteroids (including Dinkinesh and Donaldjohanson) and six Jupiter Trojans. These swarms of asteroids share Jupiter's orbit and are believed to be pristine remnants of the original primordial solar nebula.

specs.distance: Over 6.4 billion kilometers total mission path
specs.targets: Dinkinesh, Donaldjohanson, Eurybates, Polymele, Leucus, Orus, Patroclus-Menoetius
specs.milestone: Discovered satellite Selam orbiting Dinkinesh during 2023 test flyby

timeline.detail: Atlas V liftoff from Cape Canaveral
Successful rehearsal flyby revealing contact binary moon
Slingshot toward Jupiter's L4 Trojan swarm
Four consecutive close asteroid encounters
Encounter with giant Trojan binary system
